newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank plans new provisioning regulations.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank plans new provisioning regulations.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) tentatively approved changes to its regulations for risk rating of banks' debtors to try to meet international lenders' demands for boosting financial discipline, a BNB official said.

"The changes were worked out in line with recommendations by the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank for improving classification and provisioning of banks' assets," the BNB official told Reuters.
Rating of banks' debtors based on their annual balance sheets and then certified by an auditor would be among basic criteria for tclassifying the credits the banks have extended, said the official.

Perfect loans would be those that are serviced regularly or whose principal or interest payments were delayed by up to 30 days. Banks will be required to set aside three percent in provisions against such credits.
Risk debts would be divided into three groups, depending on how long their repayment was delayed.
Provision requirements of 25, 50 and 75 percent would be set for loans whose repayment was delayed by up to 90 days, up to 180 days and up to 360 days, respectively.
Loans whose principal and interest payments have been delayed by more than 360 days would be considered unperforming and would have to be 100 percent covered by provisions.
Currently, banks have to set aside 20, 50 and 100 percent in provisions against loans whose repayment was delayed by up to 60 days, up to 90 days and over 90 days, respectively.

"The longer periods under the planned new classification criteria would allow more realistic conditions for banks to collect their debts under the current unfavourable economic situation in Bulgaria," said the official.
Under the planned amendments to the BNB regulations, provisions would be entered as expenditures in banks' balance sheets in line with international accounting standards, the official said.

Provisions against local banks' nonperforming loans have been considered part of their pre-tax profit, which masked losses and led to unrealistic presentations of their financial state, said the official.

Under the planned amendments, Bulgarian banks would be required to meet the new provision requirements by April 15 on the basis of their financial results for the first quarter. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
